We Without Wings I really loved that show and how it ended. I understand that it can be confusing, but I thought it tied everything up nicely.

Speed Grapher is another that comes to mind. I really enjoyed the themes the show tackled and the characters are really well done. It is one of my favorite animes that I have watched.

Sayonara Zetsubou Sensei.

I am a huge fan of dry humor, language puns and reference to modern society. This show is full of bilingual puns (including those for character names) and lampoons a central 'theme' that is causing the main character to be in despair. Everything from Japanese politics, NEET lifestyle and Commodore Perry are all fair game.

I'm a fan of comedy shows in general that don't pander to the ecchi forms (e.g. I saw your pantsu lol, so embarrassed) or use in your face loud comedy. This show fit the bill for me.

Future Boy Conan. I'm surprised by how little attention the show has gotten considering its showrunner and lead animator is famed Hayao Miyazaki. I guess the biggest part is that it's never gotten an official English release, ever. I know that its fondly remembered by Arabic-speaking anime fans. On that note, anyone interested in either Miyazaki or Isao Takahata's animation should also check out Prince of the Sun: Hols's Great Adventure (Taiyou no Ouji: Horusu no Daibouken)..

Future Boy Conan is a children's show, but that doesn't stop it from being a sincere work about the tenacity of youth and human resilience. The closest anime recently made that I can compare it to is Erin the Beast-Player (which is something you should also watch). Nahoko Uehashi, the writer of the original Beast Player novels was about fifteen when the show aired, so I wouldn't be surprised if it had an impact on her fiction works.

Australian dairy farmer vows to continue providing raw milk despite possible $50k fine

As much as I am pro 'real food', raw dairy products, specially in a place like Australia, is something I can not abide by.

We have such long distances to transport and bottle these products, mostly in temperate heats, that bacterial growth will happen. Listeria petrifies me, and it should any parent of a child, or pregnant woman.

In a country like, say, Denmark, where the dairy farms are close by and the climate is cool, I would probably be ok with this. But drinking things like cows milk in Australia is not exactly 'natural' for our environment. Sure, don't homogenize the milk, it tastes better that way and you get the good fats... but you're not doing any damage to the milk by heating it to the point where it kills off deadly bacteria.

Your concerns are quite valid. The key to healthy success for this movement is shortening the distances of transport. Creating local outlets for those that do choose to drink raw milk. And food safety practices that insure it.

I am in Hawaii and have a local farmers market weekly that supplies my raw milk and cheese needs less than a mile away from my home. All of the farmers I buy from are extremely diligent on food and milk safety.

It's a matter of personal choice. IMO having that choice is important. Not feeling like a criminal for buying an unprocessed milk. I grew up drinking raw milk, my children have also. As have most of our neighbors and community.

It'd be interesting to see a worldwide study of cases of listeria or E. coli in raw milk and cheeses vs. processed. And even elaborating on that study, cases of food borne illness in processed packaged foods vs. those direct from farmers. Itd be interesting.
